* About the author

Beverley Trounce

BEV TROUNCE is a qualified librarian and archivist. Her father was a miner. During the 1980s she worked in a coal-mining area in Nottinghamshire where she witnessed the hardships endured by miners.

‘Conscience money’ from the south-east? It always irritates me when writers completely ignore the fact that Kent was suffering too – and it happens a lot. The county’s collieries were earmarked for closure just like everywhere else. The striking Kent miners were extremely militant, voting not to return to work after the strike in support of sacked comrades. I heard very many stories of poverty from Kent striking miners and their wives when researching for my book about the strike (‘From a Rock to a Hard Place: Memories of the Miners’ Strike’, 1985)
